description: AI-generated content can look real but still be fake. Misinformation spreads fast when people don’t fact-check. Always verify claims with trusted sources. A quick search can prevent false information from shaping your decisions. Be skeptical, question everything, and rely on credible sources. - How can you detect AI-generated misinformation? - What are the best fact-checking methods for online content? - Why is AI-generated misinformation so convincing? #misinformation #fakenews #factchecking #aiethics #criticalthinking
transcript: AI can make fake info sound super convincing. Just because something looks real doesn't mean it is. Next time you see a wild claim, stop and fact check. A quick Google search or checking trusted sources can save you from falling for fake AI generated content. Stay sharp. Don't be fooled.

description: 11/4/25 AI Garbage - CocaCola just posted their holiday ad entirely done with AI. It was very impressive but with these new tools anyone can create anything and post anything of low creativity and quality. Social media is becoming full of garbage
transcript: So this morning I read an article that said Coca-Cola just posted their new holiday ad and it was entirely made out of AI. And I was like, this is going to be terrible. And I watched it and it was like really well done. It was like an animation with animals, like Christmas themed. And they did a really good job. And it's crazy to see that AI can do stuff like that and how easily accessible it is. Big companies can do it, yes. But also like I can do it. Individuals can't. And while that's great, it takes, I think it takes a lot of the creativity out of like what social media has become. Like, I feel like it used to be so fun and like just funny. And now I feel like social media is just flooded with like AI, just garbage stuff. And then a ton of ads, which is terrible. And then there's like a few good posts now and like a few interesting things. And like my social media use has just plummeted down. It used to be like a considerable amount of time. And like, I enjoyed like sitting at night, like scrolling through some stuff, catching up, getting a good laugh. And that's like gone now. Like there's no entertainment anymore. It's just like garbage, like just more and more content of just garbage. Cause anyone can do it. And you make a video with AI, like, oh, this is cool. I'll share it. And then 20 other people do the same thing. And there was just no quality anymore. All the people that are making like actually quality stuff are just not seen because there's just so much garbage. and I think social media is going to fall off because of it and I know Casey Neistat made a video about it and just how there's like a funnel of content and then out of that funnel there's like good content and with all these advances in technology the funnel just keeps getting larger and larger and larger and to the point where your creativity can be zero you can still make something and post it doesn't mean it doesn't mean it's good but you can still post it and then you have to funnel through all of that garbage to find like decent stuff this is just the beginning of the ai creation era so i'm i'm worried a lot of a lot of garbage ahead

description: We are living through one of the most critical points in our history for art and creation. In the face of AI, monetization from big corporations, and censorship, artists are struggling more than ever to create truly independent, creatively liberated, works of art for the masses. It is becoming nearly impossible to dream of living a self-sustained life as a full-time creator, without forms of exploitation or offering up full authority and authenticity over your art. Yet, in the midst of a monetization crisis of the arts, more than ever people are clamoring for a return to media free from sponsorships and advertisements. We see more and more substance for the sole purpose of profit. Art is intrinsically tied to our humanity; it is self-expression from the soul. When such expressions are being muzzled with money and power, the end result is rot - the "art" becoming a corpse but pretending to be alive, like a marionette puppet being controlled by its strings. description: The Real Reason Companies Are Blaming Layoffs on AI AI layoffs in 2026 are not really about AI automation at all. Corporate executives respond to incentives, and announcing AI job cuts is the cleanest way to pair excess headcount reductions with a share price bump the street will reward. Whether the AI automation underneath the claim actually works is beside the point. ⏱️ CHAPTERS 0:00 AI gives executives a new playbook 0:12 Results do not matter, the claim does 0:20 What AI layoffs really are 0:33 The share price bump reward 📩 Subscribe to my newsletter: https://www.brennanmcdonald.com #AILayoffs #AIAutomation #CorporateAI
transcript: People respond to incentives, and one of the things that AI gives corporate executives is an opportunity to look at any project and think about, well, how can we use AI to make this faster, better, and cheaper? Whether it actually works out like that doesn't really matter, because as long as they can make that claim and back it up somehow, they're going to make the play.
